# dsh-water-reminder
A **hydration and posture reminder** plugin for DeepSeek Harness.
People forget to drink while they are deep in work — and just as often forget to stand up. While a s
ession is live this plugin runs **two independent reminder tracks**, and delivers each reminder thro
ugh three independent channels — missing one still leaves two:
| Track | What it nudges about | Default rhythm |

| 💧 Hydration | Today's intake and how much is left | every **40–60 minutes, drawn at random** |
| 🚶
Movement | Standing up and stretching, moving around, looking into the distance (eye strain) | ever
y **45–70 minutes, drawn at random** |
| Channel | How it lands | Needs |
| 🖥️ OS notification | `osascript` on macOS, a WinRT toast on Windows, `notify-send` on Linux | `ctx

.subprocess` (part of dsh-base) |
| 💬 In-conversation nudge | a plugin message injected into every l

ive root session, so the assistant says one line | the `agents` service |
| 🔔 Browser notification |
the sidebar panel watches `reminderSeq` and the tab raises its own notification | page open + user
panel watches `reminderSeq` and the tab raises its own notification | page open + user permission |
The two tracks keep their own rhythm, their own on/off switch, and their own state — **pausing one l
eaves the other running**. Plus a **sidebar countdown panel**, a **settings page**, and an embedded
`hydration-coach` **skill**.
## Why 40–60 at random
The irregularity is the point. A perfectly regular timer is what teaches people to ignore it — which
is why "drink water on the hour" apps get switched off. Redrawing the interval from the band on eve
ry reminder keeps the rhythm unpredictable, which is what makes it work.
The movement track works the same way, and it also draws the *reminder content*: stand up and stretc
h, move around, or look into the distance. Random, so the nudge does not decay into one repeated sen
e around, or look into the distance. Random, so the nudge does not decay into one repeated sentence.

Then reload the harness. On DeepSeek Harness ≥ 0.2.1-alpha.3 with hot reload enabled, code updates t
o this plugin apply without a restart; a fresh install (and toggling the load-time switches `promptS
ection` / `skill`) still needs one — restart `dsh web`. Never keep two `water-reminder` rows in one
profile — each would start its own timer and register the `/water/api` prefix route, and the duplica
te route makes the whole plugin tree fail to boot.
> Recreating a profile with `dsh … --from-default-profile` **replaces** that profile, including its
plugins — re-add the plugin afterwards.
## Tools
### Hydration track
| Tool | Purpose |
| `water_status` | Today's intake, remaining, cups, goal streak, current band, quiet hours, next rem

inder, 7-day series |
| `water_log` | Record a cup (defaults to the configured cup size; accepts `mi

lliliters` and `note`). Append-only, never deduplicated |
| `water_snooze` | Defer the next reminder

; defaults to 5 minutes |
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations
- **Reminders only exist while Harness is alive.** There is no email, SMS, or push channel. With the

process down, only the OS notification path exists — and only while it is up.
- **The Windows toast
needs WinRT**, invoked as `powershell -EncodedCommand` (UTF-16LE base64) so quoting and CJK text ar
e safe. If PowerShell is restricted by policy the reminder degrades to a log line, while the other t

wo channels still fire.
- **Browser notifications need a user gesture** to request permission; the 🔔

control in the panel is that gesture.
- **The 7-day series is panel-only.** `water_status` returns

a compact one-line text form instead, which keeps the tool's output schema free of nested arrays.
-
**The movement track counts breaks, not duration.** `posture_log` records "you took a break", not ho
w long it lasted or how many rounds. Finer tracking needs its own tool.
